subject: RE: Lift PCB Enquiry - Design and manufacture - SQR-45454
body_content:
You don't often get email from conor.lagrue@newburyinnovation.co.uk. Learn why this is important

Hi Giles,

Your enquiry has passed to the Innovation division of Newbury Electronics.

We have reviewed the feasibility study and representative control drawings and, in principle, this is well within our electronics design and manufacturing capability.

Before we put an indicative development range around it, there are a few points we would like to clarify as they materially affect the architecture, development effort and verification required:

  • Is Option A your intended baseline, with all safety functions and safety-related conductors remaining physically outside the PCB?
  • Specifically, can the safety-switched 24 V rail remain outside the PCB, or do you expect that rail to be distributed through it?
  • Do you want the existing Murrelektronik MICO electronic protection functionality incorporated onto the PCB, or would retaining this as a discrete component be acceptable?
  • Is the first-generation objective principally to consolidate the existing wiring, terminations and interface components around the Siemens LOGO!, rather than address the LOGO! I/O capacity limit?
  • For the first iteration, are you looking for a populated and electrically tested PCB assembly, or a complete DIN/carrier-mounted module with a dedicated production functional test fixture?
  • Should the first-generation board remain essentially an interface/distribution assembly, or do you expect any communications or remote diagnostic capability?
  • Do you have an estimate of the current panel build and test hours, or the assembly/service time you are targeting to remove? This would also help us assess the commercial case against the likely NRE.

Our initial view is that the concept is entirely feasible, but the answers above will materially change both the sensible design boundary and the development cost.

Once we have those points clarified, we can give you a meaningful indicative NRE range before either side commits significant engineering time to the detailed architecture. If that range aligns with your expectations then a call would be the next step.

Best

C

 

​Conor La Grue

​​​​​

Managing Director Newbury Innovation

E: conor.lagrue@newburyinnovation.co.uk

O: +44 (0) 1635 953493

 

 

 

From: Purchasing - Sesame Access <purchasing@sesameaccess.com>
Sent: 22 September 2026 15:56
To: Enquiries <enquiries@newburyelectronics.co.uk>
Subject: Lift PCB Enquiry - Design and manufacture - SQR-45454

 

Hello, 

 

I am contacting you on behalf of Sesame Access Systems, a UK manufacturer of platform lifts for wheelchair access.

We are investigating whether part of our existing DIN-rail lift control assembly could be replaced with a custom PCB. The aim is to reduce wiring, assembly time, build cost and servicing time while retaining the existing Siemens LOGO! 8 PLC and keeping the established safety functions outside the PCB.

Our anticipated requirement is:

  • Five initial prototypes
  • A first production batch of approximately 25 units
  • Ongoing demand of approximately 50 units per year
  • PCB design, manufacture, assembly and functional testing

I have attached our feasibility study and a representative wiring diagram. These outline the existing control system, proposed PCB scope, technical requirements, expected volumes and key design considerations.

At this stage, we are looking for an experienced partner to provide an initial feasibility opinion, recommend a suitable architecture and provide indicative NRE and unit-cost estimates.

If this project is within your capabilities, we would welcome an introductory Teams meeting with your design and manufacturing team.

 

Many Thanks,

 

Giles

Purchasing Manager
